      "observed": "D2 (red LED) has its anode (pin 2) on Net-(D2-A), which is driven only by U27.4 (Y output of an SN74LVC1G07, an open-drain buffer). Its cathode (pin 1) goes through R31 to GND (R31.1 is on the GND net). Nothing pulls the anode up to a supply, so the LED can never be forward-biased.",
      "expected": "The open-drain output should sink the LED cathode, with the anode fed from +3V3 through the current-limit resistor. This matches the other indicator LEDs driven by the same buffer type: D1, D12 and D17 have their anodes on +3V3 and their cathodes on the buffer output.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "Net-(D2-A) : D2.2(A,passive) U27.4(Y,output)"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "Net-(D2-K) : D2.1(K,passive) R31.2(2,passive)"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "GND [High Power] : ... R31.1(1,passive) ..."},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "Net-(D12-A) : D12.2(A,passive) R13.2(passive)"}
      ],
      "impact": "The D2 status LED never illuminates, so the status indication it is meant to show is lost.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["D30", "R60"],
      "pins": ["D30.2", "D30.4", "R60.1", "R60.2"],
      "nets": ["Net-(D30-K2)", "ESTOP_OUT"],
      "observed": "The second LED of dual LED D30 has its anode (D30.4, A2) on ESTOP_OUT, and its cathode (D30.2, K2) goes through R60 back to ESTOP_OUT (R60.2 is on ESTOP_OUT). The LED and its series resistor form a loop across a single net, so no current can flow and the LED is dead.",
      "expected": "The LED cathode should go to a defined sink such as GND through its series resistor, as LED1 does through R59. The anode should be on the e-stop output net, so the LED can indicate the e-stop state.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "Net-(D30-K2) : D30.2(K2,input) R60.1(passive)"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R60 Net-_D30-K2_ ESTOP_OUT 130"}
      ],
      "impact": "The second e-stop indicator LED in D30 never lights, so one e-stop status indication is missing. The e-stop chain itself is not affected.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The e-stop, CAN, power and clock connectivity checks out, but two indicator LED circuits look electrically non-functional: D2 is wired with its anode on an open-drain output and no pull-up, and one LED of D30 has both ends on ESTOP_OUT. Both are reported with moderate-to-low confidence."
}

anomalies.observed: D2 (red LED) has its anode (pin 2) on Net-(D2-A), which is driven only by U27.4 (Y output of an SN74LVC1G07, an open-drain buffer). Its cathode (pin 1) goes through R31 to GND (R31.1 is on the GND net). Nothing pulls the anode up to a supply, so the LED can never be forward-biased.
anomalies.expected: The open-drain output should sink the LED cathode, with the anode fed from +3V3 through the current-limit resistor. This matches the other indicator LEDs driven by the same buffer type: D1, D12 and D17 have their anodes on +3V3 and their cathodes on the buffer output.
anomalies.impact: The D2 status LED never illuminates, so the status indication it is meant to show is lost.

anomalies.observed: The second LED of dual LED D30 has its anode (D30.4, A2) on ESTOP_OUT, and its cathode (D30.2, K2) goes through R60 back to ESTOP_OUT (R60.2 is on ESTOP_OUT). The LED and its series resistor form a loop across a single net, so no current can flow and the LED is dead.
anomalies.expected: The LED cathode should go to a defined sink such as GND through its series resistor, as LED1 does through R59. The anode should be on the e-stop output net, so the LED can indicate the e-stop state.
